name: Ugly Brown
lede: Ugly Brown is a dark, olive-leaning [[brown]] from the xkcd 2010 crowd-name survey, one of several judgmental names ordinary respondents volunteered rather than a modifier of another word.

sections.title: A judgment, not a description
sections.body:
The 2010 xkcd survey let respondents type any name for a swatch, and a number of them reached for blunt opinions like this one instead of a hue word; who first used it beyond the survey is undocumented [1]. The ISCC-NBS block for the region reads "light olive" [1].

Our library also records Khaki Brown as a near-duplicate of this swatch, within rounding of the same color [1]. Its closest standing colors are [[hazel]], 5.0 units away by CIEDE2000 and almost the same, [[spanish-bistre]] at 5.2, duller, and [[olive]] at 6.2, duller still [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. A 2010 crowd-survey name has no particular reason to match an older painter's palette, and our archive's early centuries are thin too, so the absence is unsurprising rather than conclusive [3]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 47, chroma 53 and hue 97 degrees, a dark, strongly yellow-green-leaning brown [3].
